subject: Suppressing useless legends with I() or legend.position="none" in qplot

messages.author: a270285f50eb4297
messages.subject: Suppressing useless legends with I() or legend.position="none" in qplot
parts:
Hi All,

 

When using qplot and adjusting size, transparency, etc. I’m used to suppressing the useless legends that result but adding +opts(legend.position="none"). I finally realized that the I() function can prevent the legend from occurring in the first place. However, in ggplot, which I prefer, these legends do not occur in the first place. Can someone please explain what I() is doing and why it is needed only with qplot? I tried to search on this topic but could not find any previous discussions.

 

Thanks,

Bob

 

Here are some dotplots that yield almost identical results (+/- the legends):

 

# This will  create a legend saying simply 0=4, where 0 is the symbol of size 4.

 

qplot(workshop, stat="bin",

     facets=gender~., geom="point", size=4 ) +

  coord_flip()

 

# This suppresses that legend:

 

qplot(workshop, stat="bin",

     facets=gender~., geom="point", size=4 ) +

  opts(legend.position="none") +

  coord_flip()

 

# This does too, using I():

 

qplot(workshop, stat="bin",

     facets=gender~., geom="point", size=I(4) ) +

  coord_flip()

 

# This doesn’t do the legend, but I’m not using I(4) in it:

 

ggplot(mydata100,

   aes(workshop, ..count.. ) ) +

   geom_point(stat="bin", size=4) + coord_flip()+

   facet_grid( gender~. )

messages.subject: RE: Suppressing useless legends with I() or legend.position="none" in qplot
parts:
Hi All,

 

Here’s Hadley’s explanation of why qplot and ggplot differ on the use of the I() function :

 

When you manually add layers, it's possible to distinguish between

setting and mapping by the position of the argument - if it's in the

aes call then it maps, otherwise it sets.  You can't make this

distinction with qplot, so the additional device of I() is needed to

identified where setting behaviour is desired.

 

Cheers,

Bob
